question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

- ${max}_{x\in S}f(x)$ is the largest output value, while

- $\operatorname{arg}⁡{max}_{x\in S}f(x)$ is an input in $S$ where that largest output occurs.

On the other hand,

- ${min}_{x\in S}f(x)$ is the smallest output value, while

- $\operatorname{arg}⁡{min}_{x\in S}f(x)$ is an input in $S$ where that smallest output occurs.

Here, the outputs are $-11,$ $-5,$ $2,$ and $12.$ 

- The largest output is $12,$ and it occurs at $x=0.$

- The smallest output is $-11,$ and it occurs at $x=3.$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{max}_{x\in S}f(x) & =12 \\ \operatorname{arg}⁡{max}_{x\in S}f(x) & =0 \\ {min}_{x\in S}f(x) & =-11 \\ \operatorname{arg}⁡{min}_{x\in S}f(x) & =3\end{aligned}
$$
